title: Open rulings before the new pipeline can deploy
background: Deploying the new version of the classification pipeline, and with it restarting data-collection waves 6 and 7, waits on a chain of tasks that need your rulings. This page collects the rulings still open in the merged plan of 2 November and the latest preparation report. Where the plan wrote no options, you are offered only "state your ruling" or "defer"; nothing was drafted for you. Two questions from the brief are left out because you already ruled them: the token safety margin (uniform 90%, 2 November) and the five stopped combination fields, including the missing relation order (30 October, with the codebook re-signed).

sources.label: Merged plan, exported from origin/main 50809aa (line numbers below refer to this copy)
S5: PLAN.md:397 (agreement check awaiting PI); deltas/RC-D-006.md:22
P1: HANDOFF.txt para 2 (labelling pages, blank labels)
Already ruled: margin PLAN.md:1156 + archive/records/DP007-PI-ruling.json; stopped fields PLAN.md:1162 + deltas/RC-D-005.md:30,52; notice channel PLAN.md:2991-2992

items.title: How should the quote-matching examples be split into tuning and held-out sets?
items.situation: To choose how closely a quoted sentence must match its page, labelled examples are split into a part used to tune the cutoff and a held-out part used to report honest error rates. The 331 recovered examples are grouped by institution, as you decided, but no split has been approved and the plan proposes none.
sources: HANDOFF.txt para 2: 'Holdout allocation has not been approved'

options.label: State my ruling
options.mechanism: You describe the split in the comments box; it is recorded as written.
options.benefits: Unblocks the error-rate calculation once labels exist.
options.risks: A split set before labelling cannot react to how the labels turn out.
options.commits_to: The held-out errors being computed on the split you describe.

options.label: Defer
options.mechanism: The split stays open until you ask for drafted options or rule later.
options.benefits: Keeps the choice open until labels are in.
options.risks: The matcher, and everything after it up to the deploy, stays blocked.

items.title: One quote-match cutoff for all writing systems, or one per writing system?
items.situation: After labelling, a similarity cutoff is chosen for accepting a quote as present on its page. The recovered examples are mostly Latin script (262), with 63 Chinese/Japanese/Korean and 6 Thai, which does not by itself show language coverage. The choice of similarity measure has no drafted options; if you want to set it now, use the comments box.
sources: PLAN.md:236 (gate: PI approves metric and threshold)

options.label: One cutoff for all
options.mechanism: A single cutoff applies to every page; this is the plan's stated default.
options.benefits: Simple to state, document and audit.
options.risks: May accept false matches or reject true ones in scripts with few examples.
options.commits_to: Reporting one cutoff in the methods, whatever the per-script errors.

options.label: Per-script cutoffs where needed
options.mechanism: Use one cutoff, and add separate ones only for scripts where the held-out errors show the single cutoff fails.
options.benefits: Adapts to scripts where matching behaves differently.
options.risks: Thai has 6 examples, too few to tune a separate cutoff reliably.
options.commits_to: Letting held-out error rates decide whether per-script cutoffs appear.

items.title: Who prepares the question and prompt wording for your approval, and when?
items.situation: The plan requires your approval of any question wording for the coding model that is not copied word for word from the signed codebook, and of the two extraction prompts. Signed source files are assembled, but nothing has been packaged for your approval and the plan does not name who prepares it.
sources: Preparation-next-stage.md: 'Live stage prompts and executed configuration are not installed'

options.label: State my ruling
options.mechanism: You name who drafts the approval packet and when, in the comments box.
options.benefits: The three build tasks know when wording will be settled.
options.risks: None beyond the time it commits you to.
options.commits_to: Reviewing the packet when it arrives.

options.label: Approve later
options.mechanism: The builds go ahead and stop before merge until you approve the text.
options.benefits: No commitment now.
options.risks: Approval could land late and hold up the merge.

items.title: What cap on followed links per institution?
items.situation: Link following stops at a per-institution cap you set. The cost test was meant to measure how many links pages lead to but could not: only 3 of its 50 pages had activities and links were not yet stored. No cap values are proposed; the link-following build can use a placeholder but must stop before merge until you set one.

options.label: State my ruling
options.mechanism: You give a cap, or say how it should be measured first, in the comments box.
options.benefits: Lets the build merge without waiting for a new measurement.
options.risks: A value set without fan-out data may cut coverage or let cost grow.
options.commits_to: The cap you state, until a delta changes it.

options.label: Defer
options.mechanism: The cap stays open until fan-out is measured or you ask for options.
options.benefits: The value can rest on evidence.
options.risks: The build cannot merge, so the deploy waits.

items.title: Do the extraction steps run by the cheaper model stay in the pipeline?
items.situation: On 31 October you ruled that this would be decided after a free offline check of how often the cheaper extraction model (Claude Haiku) agrees with the main coding model. The plan records the check as done that day and awaiting your decision, and no later ruling was found. I did not open the check report, which is on Drive; the plan drafts no options.

options.label: State my ruling
options.mechanism: You rule in the comments box after reading the agreement report.
options.benefits: Closes the cost-test task, which three later tasks wait on.
options.risks: None beyond the reading time.

options.label: Defer
options.mechanism: The question stays open.
options.benefits: No commitment now.
options.risks: The cost-test task stays open, and so do the tasks after it.

items.title: How should the missing record of the round-10 wording re-test be treated?
items.situation: For the small paid wording re-test (round 10), the saved answers, request IDs, token counts and cost arithmetic all reproduce offline. The exact command that was run has not been found in the records searched, and the $0.23 saved estimate and $0.2155 recomputed cost are not invoice evidence. The plan requires command, estimate and actual cost before the task closes, and the question-set build waits on it.

options.label: State my ruling
options.mechanism: You say in the comments box how the gap is recorded or closed.
options.benefits: Lets the re-test task close on terms you set.
options.risks: None beyond the time.

options.label: Defer
options.mechanism: The task stays open until the command is found or you rule.
options.benefits: Leaves room for a further search.
options.risks: The question-set build, and so the deploy, stays blocked.

items.title: Open a new display window for runs after 1 January 2027?
items.situation: The website shows ordinary runs only if they start inside an open wave window, and only you open new ones. The current window ends 1 January 2027, and waves 6 and 7 run after the deploy, so any run starting after that date would not appear without a new window. The plan drafts no window dates.

options.label: State my ruling
options.mechanism: You give the new window's dates in the comments box.
options.benefits: Waves 6 and 7 stay visible whenever they run.
options.risks: None beyond setting the dates.

options.label: Defer
options.mechanism: Decide at the reminder (see P11).
options.benefits: Dates can follow the actual deploy date.
options.risks: If the reminder slips, new runs could silently disappear from the site.

items.title: When will the quote-matching examples be labelled, and by whom?
items.situation: Two labelling pages are ready: one for the main labels on all 331 examples and a blind page for your independent check of 30 of them. All labels are still blank; the matcher cutoff, the website quote cap and the tasks after them wait on these labels. The plan does not say who does the main labels.

options.label: State the schedule
options.mechanism: You give who labels and by when in the comments box.
options.benefits: The matcher work can be timed.
options.risks: None.

options.label: Defer
options.mechanism: Scheduling stays open.
options.benefits: No commitment now.
options.risks: The matcher stays blocked.

items.title: How should candidate lengths for the website quote cap be proposed?
items.situation: The website shows a shortened quote with access to the full text; you set the length. The plan asks how the agent should present candidate lengths once quote lengths are measured.

options.label: Propose the 90% length
options.mechanism: Propose the length that covers 90% of quotes.
options.benefits: One clear number to accept or change.
options.risks: Anchors you on one value.

options.label: Show the trade-off table
options.mechanism: Show the length distribution and the share of quotes each candidate cap would cut.
options.benefits: You see the trade-off directly.
options.risks: Slightly more to read.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation: you set the value, so the agent should show the trade-off rather than pick a number.

items.title: How many test pages per acceptance check?
items.situation: Test pages with known answers check the built pipeline before the paid test run; you label the real ones. The plan asks how many per acceptance check.

options.label: At least 3 each
options.mechanism: At least three test pages per acceptance check.
options.benefits: Keeps your labelling time small.
options.risks: Some page-verdict values may not be tested.

options.label: 3 each, plus every verdict
options.mechanism: At least three per check, and one per page-verdict value for the verdict check.
options.benefits: Every verdict value is exercised.
options.risks: A few more pages to label.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation: covers every value while keeping labelling time bounded.

items.title: When will you label the real test pages?
items.situation: The test-page set has not been built yet. Once it is, you label and approve the expected answer on every real page, and the paid test run waits on that. This is a scheduling question; the plan gives no date.

options.label: State the schedule
options.mechanism: You give a time window in the comments box.
options.benefits: The test-page builder can plan around it.
options.risks: None.

options.label: Defer
options.mechanism: Schedule when the set is built.
options.benefits: No commitment now.
options.risks: Labelling may become the last blocker before the test run.

items.title: Where do text positions count from on long pages that are split?
items.situation: Long pages are split into parts for the coding model, and the extraction step records where each activity's text sits. The plan asks what the positions count from.

options.label: From the start of the whole page
options.mechanism: Positions are offsets into the full page text (plan default).
options.benefits: Stable however the page is split.
options.risks: Each part must carry its starting offset.

options.label: Leave to the builder
options.mechanism: The engineer decides during the build.
options.benefits: No ruling needed now.
options.risks: The next step may assume a different base.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation: full-page positions stay stable, and the next step marks text on the full page.

items.title: One supporting-text request per page, or one per activity?
items.situation: The second extraction call fetches supporting text for each activity on a page. The plan asks whether to send one request per page covering all its activities or one per activity.

options.label: One per page
options.mechanism: One request covers all of a page's activities (plan default).
options.benefits: Fewer batch requests.
options.risks: Large pages with many activities may hit size limits.

options.label: One per activity
options.mechanism: One request per page-and-activity pair.
options.benefits: Each request stays small.
options.risks: More requests and repeated page text.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation: fewer requests; switch only if size limits bite.

items.title: Deliver the database and website spec as one issue per task, or one per repository?
items.situation: The interface spec for Colin goes out as GitHub issues. The approved spec and the three unsent drafts already follow one issue per task, but the plan never records an explicit ruling. Sending still needs your separate instruction and a link Colin can open.

options.label: One per task
options.mechanism: Two issues on the API repository and one on the website repository, each linking the spec.
options.benefits: Each task's acceptance is tracked separately; drafts already exist.
options.risks: Three threads to follow.

options.label: One per repository
options.mechanism: One umbrella issue per repository.
options.benefits: Fewer threads.
options.risks: Acceptance of separate tasks blurs together; drafts must be merged.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation, and it matches the approved spec and the existing drafts.

items.title: Is the 'latest row' table a live view or a stored copy?
items.situation: The API shows each institution's most recent row through a database view. The plan asks whether it is computed on each query or stored and refreshed.

options.label: Live view
options.mechanism: Computed on each query (plan default).
options.benefits: Always current; no refresh step.
options.risks: Could be slow at scale.

options.label: Stored copy
options.mechanism: A materialized view refreshed on demand.
options.benefits: Fast reads.
options.risks: Another refresh step that can go stale.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation: start live; store a copy only if the rehearsal shows slow responses.

items.title: How does the API expose older rows?
items.situation: Older rows stay available after a newer one replaces them. The plan asks whether they come through an option on the existing endpoints or a separate history endpoint.

options.label: Option on existing endpoints
options.mechanism: A query parameter on the institution endpoints (plan default).
options.benefits: One surface to document and test.
options.risks: Existing endpoints grow more complex.

options.label: Separate history endpoint
options.mechanism: A new endpoint just for older rows.
options.benefits: Keeps current endpoints unchanged.
options.risks: More endpoints to document and test.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation: one contract surface, fewer endpoints.

items.title: Before loading corrections, snapshot the live database how?
items.situation: Before corrected rows are loaded into the live database, a snapshot is taken for rollback. This happens after the deploy, so it does not block it.

options.label: Database branch
options.mechanism: A free, instant branch of the live database, named for the date (plan default).
options.benefits: Instant and restorable.
options.risks: Depends on the hosting provider.

options.label: Full export file
options.mechanism: A full database dump to a file.
options.benefits: Independent of the provider.
options.risks: Slower to take and restore.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation: instant and restorable; the provider's point-in-time restore was not verified.

items.title: When should the agent check and remind you about the display window?
items.situation: The current display window ends 1 January 2027 (see S7). The plan sets a check-and-remind date so new runs do not silently disappear.

options.label: 1 December 2026
options.mechanism: Check the live window and remind you on 1 December (plan default).
options.benefits: A month's margin.
options.risks: None.

options.label: Defer
options.mechanism: No date set now.
options.benefits: None.
options.risks: The reminder may be missed.

recommendation.reason: The plan's recommendation: a month's margin before new runs would vanish from the site.
